text:
Olga: quick heads-up — customer reported they can see other tenant IDs in the audit viewer. Screenshot coming.
Raj: yikes. can you paste the screenshot or sample event?
Olga: see attached (screenshot). they pointed at the "target" field showing tenant: xyz-123 in multiple events from different orgs.
Sam: have we verified whether the indexing pipeline tags tenant IDs as searchable metadata? if so ES query perms might be leaking.
Maya: from compliance POV, scoped visibility is required: members should only see events scoped to their tenant; admins may see cross-tenant only if permitted under contract.
Raj: digging in logs — looks like our audit-ingest service writes raw event.payload to index and sets tenant_id as a top-level string. no scope ACL applied at index time.
Olga: hmm. did we recently change the schema? I remember a proposal to flatten actor/target fields for easier queries.
Ava: yes we flattened. proposal PR: https://gh/repo/pulls/4123 — the flattening added tenant_id at top-level for search perf. probably this.
Sam: this explains it. we did it to speed filtering but forgot to pair with per-index ACL or doc-level security.
SecurityBot: INCIDENT CREATED #INC-2026-241 - potential tenant visibility leak. owner=olga severity=high
Raj: immediate mitigations: 1) roll back flattening OR 2) add doc-level ACL on ES that denies cross-tenant reads for non-admin tokens. which is faster?
Sam: adding doc-level ACL needs mapping + reindex, slow. rollback PR is quick but disruptive. we can also add an access-layer filter in the audit service to strip tenant_id on non-admin tokens while we decide.
Maya: we need to notify impacted customers and trigger DSR playbook if any data exfiltration. legal is on standby.
Olga: agreed. propose short-term: access-layer masking for member tokens + hotfix to search API to apply tenant filter by token scope. long-term: change schema to include "scope": {"actor_tenant": "...", "target_tenant": "..."} and keep top-level tenant_id removed.
Raj: sample event we could validate customer-facing: 
```
{
  "event": "model.deploy",
  "actor": {"id":"u-123","tenant":"t-A"},
  "target": {"id":"m-987","tenant":"t-A"},
  "meta": {"request_id":"r-456"},
  "scope": {"actor_tenant":"t-A","target_tenant":"t-A"}
}
```
Raj: note: don't expose internal tenant UUIDs in the public viewer. maybe present a hash or alias per-tenant.
Ava: question: how will this interact with scoped tokens? if a scoped token is issued that elevates to cross-tenant read (support), it should include a claim like: "audit:read:tenants": ["t-A","t-B"].
Sam: yes — auth service should mint JWT with audit_read scope. search layer will evaluate token claims and return only allowed tenant docs. if missing, treat as member token and filter by token.tenant.
Maya: KMS question — audit signing currently uses per-cluster key. for customer-facing validation we need a per-tenant public key or a signing service that can provide signed proofs without revealing key material. thoughts?
Raj: we can HSM-sign the canonical event with a per-tenant key id in header: "kid": "tenant-t-A-v1" and customers can fetch public keys from our JWKS endpoint to validate events they receive.
Olga: downside: managing many tenant keys is operational overhead. alternative: sign with a platform key and include an audit-hash that customers can verify via our API which validates ownership with KMS.
Maya: legal prefers per-tenant verifiability. maybe per-tenant key material stored in KMS but rotated via infra automation. ok to scope as medium-term.
Sam: immediate action items: 
- olga: patch audit-serving to mask tenant_id for non-admin tokens (hotfix) — ETA 2h
- raj: open rollback PR for flattening + link impact analysis — ETA 4h
- ava: draft customer notification + coordinate with legal & CS — ETA 3h
- maya: start KMS feasibility doc for per-tenant signing — ETA EOD
SecurityBot: ASSIGNMENTS UPDATED incident=INC-2026-241 assignees=[Olga,Raj,Ava,Maya]
Olga: thanks team. let's sync at :45 in #eng-oncall and post updates here. :lock::eyes:
